teaser.text:
Fresnillo plc turns Mexican rock into saleable metal-bearing materials, then receives dollars from a processor. 
To understand the business, follow one shipment from the mine through pricing and collection, then follow the money back out through operating costs, investment and obligations.

stock.title: Fresnillo stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Fresnillo's weighted forecast is near-flat, while metal prices, production and mine replacement drive the bear, base and bull cases.
stock.opening: Fresnillo's weighted forecast is near-flat by October 2029. It hinges on 2027 production reaching management's ranges while cash funds capital spending without dilution.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Fresnillo's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The forecast's central message is near-flat weighted returns despite a wide operating range. The weighted price is 2548.22 GBp in October 2027, a total return of -0% including dividends. It reaches 2564.70 GBp in October 2028, a return of +4%. By October 2029 it is 2495.15 GBp, a return of +5%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Fresnillo?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires silver and gold prices to retreat before Fresnillo completes its production recovery. Lower grades, metallurgy problems, peso costs and delayed replacement projects compress margins and dividends, while the multiple falls. It reaches 1296.92 GBp in October 2027 and 869.43 GBp in October 2029. The probability is 27% because all four specialists assign meaningful downside risk, although opening net cash reduces financing stress.

The base case gains support if 2027 production reaches management's ranges and cash funds capital spending without dilution. The bull case needs improved grades and throughput, firm realized prices, and visible progress on replacement projects during 2028–2029.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Fresnillo really make?

paragraphs.text: After capital spending, lease payments and interest, free cash flow reached US$1,844,252 thousand. Earlier years consumed cash: free cash flow was negative US$150,377 thousand in 2022. Across the five years, cumulative free cash flow was US$2,693,040 thousand, most of it arriving in the final two years.

dividend.title: Fresnillo dividend
dividend.meta_description: Fresnillo’s dividend history, cash coverage, outlook and yield, explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Fresnillo’s dividend per share rose from US$0.06 in 2023 to US$1.29 in 2025. Free cash flow reached US$1,844,252 thousand in 2025, but dividends also continued when free cash flow was negative.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers how Fresnillo’s business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: How much does Fresnillo pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends follow the same cycle. Base DPS is US$1.50 in the first window, then US$1.40 and US$1.50, supported by the 50% adjusted-profit policy and production recovery. Bear DPS is US$0.50, then US$0.30 and US$0.50, while bull DPS is US$2.50, US$2.50 and US$2.80. The wide spread reflects the move from US$0.06 in 2023 to US$1.29 in 2025 and the possibility, but not certainty, of special distributions.

blocks.heading: Is Fresnillo’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: From 2021 to 2023, free cash flow fell from positive to negative, but dividends continued. In 2023, Fresnillo also repaid debt. A household can pay a bill during a low-income month from savings accumulated earlier; the payment happened, but that month’s income did not cover it. Fresnillo’s dividends similarly drew on financial resources built elsewhere or earlier.

After capital spending, lease payments and interest, free cash flow reached US$1,844,252 thousand. Earlier years consumed cash: free cash flow was negative US$150,377 thousand in 2022. Across the five years, cumulative free cash flow was US$2,693,040 thousand, most of it arriving in the final two years.

The recovery changed the choices available. By 2025, higher precious-metals prices had sharply increased cash generation. Fresnillo paid dividends, made payments to minority owners and accumulated substantial cash. Investment sales also helped rebuild liquidity, but releasing invested money is different from earning it through mining. By year-end, cash and short-term investments exceeded total debt, leaving the company with net cash.
